title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mather, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mather, PA | Greene County
metaDescription: Mather, PA sits in the core Marcellus wet-gas window of Greene County. We buy mineral and royalty interests directly, with straight talk on deductions.
heroLead: Mather is a small unincorporated community in Greene County, but the ground underneath it sits in some of the most active Marcellus wet-gas territory in the entire state.
intro: Greene County is where a lot of the Marcellus story in Pennsylvania actually plays out, and Mather, tucked in Union Township along Whiteley Creek, is squarely inside it. Operators have run pad after pad through this part of the county for over a decade, which means a lot of local families are sitting on interests that are far more active than they realize.

We buy mineral and royalty rights around Mather directly. No listing service, no shopping your interest around to strangers. We tell you what we find in the title and production records, then make a straightforward offer.

sections.heading: Union Township's Drilling History
paragraphs: Whiteley Creek and the rolling hollows around Mather have seen multi-well pads developed since the early days of the Marcellus boom, with laterals extending under old farm tracts that were subdivided among heirs long before anyone thought about horizontal drilling. If your family's land was ever part of a larger farm that got split up, there's a good chance your current interest is a fraction of what a grandparent originally owned.

Greene County sits in the wet-gas core, so production here carries natural gas liquids alongside methane, and pricing on your royalty check reflects that liquids content along with whatever the operator deducts for processing before the sale.

sections.heading: Tracing Title Through Greene County Records
paragraphs: We start with the Greene County Recorder of Deeds in Waynesburg to confirm how your interest was created and whether any prior conveyances or reservations affect what you actually own today. Rural Union Township deeds sometimes reference old farm boundaries by metes and bounds rather than modern parcel numbers, which takes patience to reconcile.
Once title is clear, we look at your division order decimal and any royalty history you can share, since actual production tells us more than a well's original announced numbers.

sections.heading: Act 13 and What It Means Locally
paragraphs: Greene County has collected impact fees under Act 13 for years, and those payments have funded real infrastructure work around communities like Mather. That's a separate stream from your personal royalty, but it's part of why so many Greene County residents have grown skeptical of promises that don't match what shows up in their own mailbox.
We'd rather be direct about what your specific interest is worth than make comparisons to county-level fee revenue that has nothing to do with your check.

faqs.question: Is Mather considered core Marcellus territory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Greene County generally, and Union Township specifically, sits in one of the most heavily developed parts of the Marcellus wet-gas window in Pennsylvania.

faqs.question: My royalty statement changes a lot month to month. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is. Marcellus wells decline quickly in their first couple years, and liquids pricing fluctuates too, so month-to-month variation on an active well is expected rather than a red flag.

faqs.question: Can you buy just part of my interest?
faqs.answer: In some cases, yes. Tell us what you're weighing and we'll explain whether a partial sale makes sense for your situation.
